parsed.explanation: The operative regime for a trans visitor is thin-data but structurally adverse. The 2024 read-down removes the main criminal lever for private adult conduct — a functioning-court positive — yet the construed provisions remain, with no sourced confirmation of forward application. Documented severity drivers: police refused to investigate a violent attack on an LGBT claimant because victims were 'criminals' (2019), victims were ridiculed (2011), violence against people perceived as gender-nonconforming is documented including a killing (2010), and effeminacy is policed by slurs. No trans-specific acceptance, healthcare record, marker rules or facility rules exist in the record; per thin-data extrapolation, absence of any documented acceptance plus documented police non-protection resolves toward risk, not midpoint. Public visitor-directed hostility ('gay tourists' should be barred) adds a targeting frame. The recent judicial trajectory, bishop's stance and dated diplomatic signature temper but do not offset. Upper High Risk band.

entry_documents.exposure: Not documented. No gender-marker, documentation or entry-screening rules for trans visitors appear in the record; mismatch-handling at borders is unknown.
entry_documents.protection: None documented. No instrument accepting foreign documents or chosen markers is cited.
entry_documents.interaction: Any passport-marker mismatch that surfaces in an incident would enter a policing system documented as treating LGBT victims as criminals.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Historical enforcement real: 35 buggery arrests 1995–2000 with prison up to ten years and psychiatric committals; 2001 group sentences of women and men for gross indecency. Custody placement rules for trans detainees are not documented.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: 2014 government statement of non-enforcement in private homes; 2024 read-down exempts private consensual adult acts.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Remedy is a reading-down, not repeal; no later appellate, legislative or executive confirmation of forward application is sourced.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Not documented. No facility-access, bathroom, ward or shelter rules appear in the record.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: If a trans visitor needed custody or hospital placement, no rule or protocol governs placement by identity; unregulated discretion applies.

care_services.exposure: Not documented. No record of trans healthcare access, HRT availability, or refusal of care; absence of evidence is not safety in a thin-data state.
care_services.interaction: Medication continuity depends on undocumented local practice; discovery during care would meet the same dismissive institutions documented elsewhere.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Documented: police refused to investigate a violent attack on the 2019 claimant because gay people 'were criminals'; victims reportedly ridiculed (2011); slurs for effeminate men; 2009 evangelical call for government to bar 'gay tourists' and protests against gay cruises.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: 2013 bishop publicly urged decriminalisation and against violence toward LGBT people; 2011 UN joint statement signed.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State is documented bystander, not protector; police hostility converts private violence into low-recourse exposure for anyone read as gender-nonconforming.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented. No rule touching a travelling minor or guardian arises from the record.
minors_guardians.interaction: An adult with a minor would face the same undocumented marker and policing environment as a solo traveller.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Documented: 2010 stabbing death of a man perceived as gay, perpetrator reportedly preaching killing gay people; suspected hate crimes recorded; violence against perceived gender-nonconforming people noted. Mostly dated; rate unverifiable.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Courts function — a constitutional challenge succeeded (2024) — but no record shows police protection or prosecution of attackers working for LGBT victims.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Documented police non-response to anti-LGBT violence leaves street hostility largely unremedied.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No anti-discrimination law on sexual orientation or gender identity; no union recognition, so a trans visitor in a locally same-sex relationship has no partner or next-of-kin standing.
remedies_unknowns.protection: 2024 high-court read-down shows courts can grant relief; 2019–2024 litigation trajectory is positive.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: No follow-on confirmation of the construed sections' application; all trans-specific treatment is unknown, not neutral.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar police-hostility tier (dismissed complaints here, dismissed oversight in Meridia) and thin recourse, but this jurisdiction documents an actual killing of a gender-nonconforming-perceived person and historical prison sentences, pushing below 0.25-B's extortion-only profile.

Karthovia documents routine trans-specific stops with bounded detention. Here no trans-specific targeting is documented, but severity after any discovery is worse: police refusal to protect victims, a killing, and a residual criminal-lever statute with enforcement history.

Vesskar has universal-exposure biometric checks with a deceptive-presentation statute. This jurisdiction lacks documented universal measures and shows a functioning court granting relief (2024) — better on probability and judicial recourse — but documented police non-protection and anti-trans-perceived violence hold it below 0.45.

parsed.synthesis: The combined regime pairs a recent judicial decriminalisation with a policing and social environment documented hostile to people read as gender-nonconforming. Severity after discovery dominates: no protections exist, police are documented refusing to investigate anti-LGBT violence, a killing is on record, and the construed criminal provisions survive as a latent lever with an enforcement history that included imprisonment and psychiatric committals of women and men. No trans-specific evidence exists anywhere in the dossier — no marker rules, facility rules, care access or acceptance record — and thin-data extrapolation from the structural facts (residual statute, dismissive police, documented violence, no documented tolerance) resolves toward risk rather than the midpoint. The 2024 ruling, judicial functionality, the bishop's stance and the dated diplomatic signature are genuine positives that keep this above the 0.25 tier, but public visitor-directed hostility and the absence of any working recourse place the jurisdiction in the upper High Risk band.
